findings.title: Negative offsets passed to Django queryset slicing raise errors / expose data
findings.body: OptimizedCursorPaginator slices the queryset with a negative start offset whenever the cursor offset is negative and advanced features are on. The cursor offset is fully client-controlled. Django querysets do not support negative indexing and raise ValueError/AssertionError, so these requests fail with a 500. The comment that the ORM 'properly handles negative slicing' is false, and the stated intent of reaching data 'beyond normal pagination bounds' is a security smell.

findings.title: BasePaginator now passes negative offsets for prev cursors
findings.body: BasePaginator previously sliced the queryset with the raw offset. It now uses an unclamped offset when `is_prev` is set. A client-supplied cursor such as `0:-5:1` sends a negative slice to the Django queryset, which raises an exception (500) on every endpoint that uses Paginator or DateTimePaginator. Clamping only for non-prev cursors gives no protection where negative offsets are actually reachable.

findings.title: OptimizedCursorPaginator breaks on datetime keys
findings.body: The audit log endpoint uses this paginator with `order_by=-datetime`. Its `get_item_key` calls `math.floor`/`math.ceil` on a datetime value, which raises TypeError. Its `value_from_cursor` returns the raw number instead of a datetime, so the generated SQL compares a timestamp column against an integer. The optimized pagination path therefore fails for every request that uses it.

findings.title: organization_context.member may be None
findings.body: For superusers or staff who are not members of the organization, `organization_context.member` is None. Because `or` short-circuits, superusers are fine. A non-superuser with no membership, for example access through other permissions, gets an AttributeError when the code reads `member.has_global_access`, and the request returns a 500.

findings.title: span_count can be stale after second zunionstore is skipped
findings.body: When only the first zunionstore runs, `span_count` is taken from it, which is fine. The eviction step uses `zpopmin`, which removes the spans with the lowest scores (the earliest end timestamps). This can evict the root/segment span, so the flushed segment loses its root and `is_segment` detection breaks. Separately, the hardcoded 1000 limit ignores the configurable `max_segment_spans`.

findings.title: __reduce__ passes redis_ttl as segment_page_size
findings.body: `__reduce__` passes its arguments positionally, so the 4th argument (`redis_ttl`) lands in the `segment_page_size` parameter. In the multiprocessing path, which pickles the buffer, worker processes therefore get a page size of 3600 and the default TTL. This bug predates the PR but becomes more relevant now that the PR changes the buffer constructor's parameters.

findings.title: No test for new eviction behavior
findings.body: The PR adds span-count eviction in Lua and removes the `max_segment_spans` check in Python. No test covers a segment that exceeds 1000 spans, so it is unverified which spans are evicted or that the root span is preserved.
